Researchers have estimated that about 9 percent of people living in the United States, or 28.8 million 
Americans, will have an eating disorder in their lifetime.4 The prevalence of eating disorders also 
seems to be increasing.5 Eating disorders can be accompanied by many health complications, and 
among all mental illnesses, eating disorders have one of the highest fatality rates. Anorexia 
nervosa in particular can be deadly; it has the second highest mortality rate of mental illnesses, 
outranked only by substance use disorder.6 Eating disorders cause approximately 10,200 deaths 
each year, or one death every 52 minutes in the United States.4 In a large study of U.S. college 
students published in 2020, those with the greatest level of eating disorder symptoms were 11 times 
more likely to have attempted suicide compared with those who did not have an eating disorder.7
